text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- The Bulgarian National Bank cut the monthly central interest rate to 20 percent from record high 25 percent, or 240 percent annually from 300 percent, effective from October 18, due to positive changes in the financial sector. @

-- There is no technical possibility for the International Monetary Fund (IMF) to extend the delayed $115 million second tranche of funding to Bulgaria by the end of October, IMF representative in Bulgaria Franek Rozwadowski said after meeting President Zhelyu Zhelev.

-- President Zhelyu Zhelev is expected to veto recent amendments to the Deposit Guarantee Law, which concern the timing for payment of deposits in insolvent banks, the president's economic advisor Kiril Velev said. @
-- Electricity prices should be frozen during the winter as they are already unaffordable for a lot of Bulgarians, Economic Development minister Roumen Gechev said.
-- Bulgaria's cabinet approved the export of some 30,000 tonnes of cooking oil at $100 per tonne export fee to raise additional funds for wheat imports, Agriculture minister Krastyo Trendafilov said.
-- A minimum 20 million lev share capital will be required to set up a commodity exchange in Bulgaria under a Commodity Exchange Law approved by parliament. @

-- A State Investment and Development Bank is to be set up to extend credits to small- and medium-size companies and for infrastructure projects under a draft bill approved by the parliament's budjet committee.
-- The U.S. oil giant Texaco plans to invest $60 million in the development of an offshore gas field in the Black Sea near Varna and building a pipeline to the coast, a company official said. @
-- Some 684,000 hectares of wheat and barley have been sown in Bulgaria this autumn so far out of 1.6 million hectares required, Agriculture Minister Krastyo Trendafilov said.
-- Some 12 billion levs have been siphoned from Bulgarian banks in the first nine months of 1996, head of Bulgaria's economic police Dimitar Moskov said. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
